items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, both sides. (1) The filed digits hold: the verse-initial imperative of שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי (oshb:Isa.33.13, tier: byte) stands verse-initial at exactly 10 MT verses book-wide, identical at skeleton and accent-stripped tiers (sweep: 10 verses, verse-initial token: MT 1:2, 1:10, 33:13, 46:3, 46:12, 48:1, 49:1, 51:1, 51:7, 66:5), one site in chs 28-35; the verse-initial hoy of ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד (oshb:Isa.33.1, tier: byte) is the sixth of the chs 28-33 woe series (sweep: 6 verses, verse-initial token at skeleton tier: MT 28:1, 29:1, 29:15, 30:1, 31:1, 33:1); the single-witness inventory carries SAMEKH at MT 33:1, 33:6 and 33:12 and nothing at 33:24, so the row's claim that its interior segs mark turns binding to no fresh vocative marker is byte-false at 33:12, whose division falls immediately before the summons, and true only at 33:6, whose next verse opens on the presentative הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.33.7, tier: byte). (2) Characterization, as instructed: the defect is INADEQUATE TREATMENT, not total omission -- the row quotes the 33:13 summons at byte tier, verifies its digit, names its formal class as that of the summons opening 34:1, and then declines it on a rule (no fresh hoy, massa or divine-frame marker) that omits the ruled imperative/vocative-summons and addressee-shift class and that, as stated, cannot discriminate 33:13 from קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (oshb:Isa.34.1, tier: byte), which carries no hoy, no massa and no koh-amar frame either (first-token and formula sweeps at skeleton tier) yet opens the neighbouring row; its scene-continuity sentence is asserted, not shown from bytes. (3) Both-sides test at the declined seam MT 33:12|33:13: the preceding side closes on וְהָי֥וּ עַמִּ֖ים מִשְׂרְפ֣וֹת שִׂ֑יד (oshb:Isa.33.12, tier: byte), third-person description whose runs stand at exactly 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier -- no refrain, no formula, so the refrain-close rule (§6) gives no close-side warrant and the SAMEKH there is tier-3 corroboration only. The onset side carries the ruled summons class (§2a: verse-initial imperative with the named addressees רְחוֹקִ֖ים and קְרוֹבִ֖ים), and the addressee does change in the bytes: 33:11 addresses a second-person plural, רוּחֲכֶ֕ם אֵ֖שׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.33.11, tier: byte), 33:12 is third-person, 33:13 summons the far and the near. The seam is therefore warranted from its onset side and the row's stated decline ground fails. (4) The ground the row could have argued and did not: the summons is bound to the divine speech opened by the postpositive signature עַתָּ֥ה אָק֖וּם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.33.10, tier: byte) through its own first-person forms עָשִׂ֑יתִי and גְּבֻרָתִֽי (oshb:Isa.33.13, tier: byte; both witnesses render first person; no morphology layer is staged), and the speaker changes only at פָּחֲד֤וּ בְצִיּוֹן֙ חַטָּאִ֔ים with מִ֣י יָג֣וּר לָ֗נוּ (oshb:Isa.33.14, tier: byte), a first-person-plural community voice; 34:1's summons carries no first-person form and continues no frame, its preceding verse וּבַל יֹאמַ֥ר שָׁכֵ֖ן חָלִ֑יתִי (oshb:Isa.33.24, tier: byte) closing in third-person description. That ground survives the tier-1 class and discriminates 33:13 from 34:1 under the frame-plus-speech default (§6). Severity: the prior adjudication confirmed high on the rule that a whole-chapter span held by a decline omitting the tier-1 class and resting on a byte-false mark-binding claim is load-bearing, on the premise that the respan is byte-sound; the complete test shows the boundary is not byte-shown wrong (a sound hold-warrant exists in the bytes, and the rear seam at 33:24 is warranted from the following unit's onset at 34:1, the ruled addressee shift to the nations), the byte-false binding claim concerns a tier-3 layer that can bear no boundary load under owner law, and the load-bearing defect is a wrongly stated decline rule: a defective warrant on a byte-sound span -- downgrade to medium. Span ruling: decline_proposal on the respan branch -- a cut at 33:12|33:13 would sever the first-person divine speech MT 33:10-13 from its own closing summons with no ruled close on the preceding side; the proposal's hold-and-re-argue branch is the remedy the bytes support and is a field repair, not a span change; a rival interior cut at the speaker shift 33:13|33:14 is disclosed as a docket question, not ruled here. Ruled coherently with the 34:1 row, whose onset stands (verse-initial imperative at exactly 3 verses book-wide at skeleton tier: MT 34:1, 41:21, 48:16).

Re-derived from bytes, both sides of the front seam MT 36:10|36:11. Preceding side: the prior unit closes on the herald's own YHWH-attribution יְהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י עֲלֵ֛ה (oshb:Isa.36.10, tier: byte), a rhetorical close standing at exactly 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier -- no refrain, no formula close, and no seg at MT 36:10 or 36:11 in the single-witness inventory (absence not counterevidence); the refrain-close rule (§6) offers nothing, so the seam depends on its onset side. Onset side: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִים֩ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה (oshb:Isa.36.11, tier: byte; the title is two tokens in the staged extract) is a verse-initial narrative speech frame with full speaker-and-addressee inversion against the frame that opened the prior unit, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה (oshb:Isa.36.4, tier: byte) -- the ruled participant/scene-shift class at which narrative_prose units cut (§6); verse-initial vayomer stands at 10 MT verses in chs 36-39 (sweep: 10 verses, verse-initial token at skeleton tier: 36:4, 36:11, 36:12, 37:6, 38:3, 38:21, 38:22, 39:4, 39:5, 39:8) and the 36:11 speaker set is unique (sweep: 1 verse, the four-token onset at skeleton tier). The row as shipped: boundary_rationale writes 'turns on an audience question rather than on a new speech frame', quotes MT 36:11 in English only, splices Hebrew only at oshb:Isa.36.12, and its boundary_evidence_refs carry no oshb:Isa.36.11 (verified programmatically against the shipped row) -- the stated warrant disclaims the only ruled signal the seam has. Collaterals re-sweep exact: the bare hiriq-pointed form אֲדֹנִ֔י (oshb:Isa.36.12, tier: byte) stands word-bound at exactly 3 verses at accent-stripped tier (MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12); it is distinct from אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ (oshb:Isa.36.12, tier: byte) at byte and skeleton tiers; MT 36:12 carries 2 ketiv/qere notes in the single-witness inventory. The filed finding diagnosed the onset side; the complete test does not change the outcome, because the preceding side carries no ruled close, leaving the disclaimed onset frame as the seam's sole tier-1 warrant. Agrees with the prior adjudication's rule (front-seam warrant defect, span right). Confirm medium; field repair as proposed, no span change.

Re-derived from bytes at the shared seam MT 40:17|40:18, both sides. The row's own close: כָּל הַגּוֹיִ֖ם כְּאַ֣יִן נֶגְדּ֑וֹ מֵאֶ֥פֶס וָתֹ֖הוּ נֶחְשְׁבוּ לֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.40.17, tier: byte) is unaddressed third person, its runs standing at exactly 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier (no refrain, no formula), so the refrain-close rule (§6) gives no close-side warrant; the single-witness inventory carries SAMEKH at MT 40:11, 40:16 and 40:24 and nothing at 40:17 (absence not counterevidence). The span is unaddressed throughout -- מִֽי מָדַ֨ד (oshb:Isa.40.12, tier: byte), מִֽי תִכֵּ֥ן (oshb:Isa.40.13, tier: byte), אֶת מִ֤י נוֹעָץ֙ (oshb:Isa.40.14, tier: byte) -- with no second-person form in MT 40:12-17 read against both witnesses' renderings (no morphology layer staged). The following unit's onset: וְאֶל מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן אֵ֑ל וּמַה דְּמ֖וּת תַּ֥עַרְכוּ לֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte) opens a second-person-plural address (web:Isa.40.18 renders both verbs as 'you'), the ruled addressee-shift class (§2a), so the rear seam is warranted from the following unit's onset under the both-sides law. The row's named ground is instead the construction contrast between the bare and the prepositional interrogative (device_notes: 'the signal that does is the shift in construction'), a class the strategy does not rule, and observed_substrate_signals carries only oracle_frame.topic_onset. The construction pair itself is honest at its tier: וְאֶל מִ֖י (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.25 at accent_stripped tier, and that two-token onset stands verse-initial at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier: MT 40:18, 40:25). The filed finding already weighed both sides (the span's unaddressed close and the next verse's address); the complete test re-derives it unchanged and agrees with the prior adjudication's rule. Boundary byte-sound, warrant on a non-ruled class: confirm medium; one seam-pair edit shared with the following row's onset item, no span change.

Same seam MT 40:17|40:18, re-derived from the onset side and ruled coherently with the preceding row's close item. Preceding unit's close: נֶחְשְׁבוּ לֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.40.17, tier: byte) ends an unaddressed third-person span with no refrain or formula (runs at exactly 1 verse book-wide, skeleton tier) and no seg at MT 40:17 -- no close-side warrant under the refrain-close rule (§6). Onset side: תְּדַמְּי֣וּן and תַּ֥עַרְכוּ (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte, each against its own verse) open a second-person-plural address absent from MT 40:12-17 and continued at הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.40.21, tier: byte) and תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי (oshb:Isa.40.25, tier: byte): the ruled addressee-shift class (§2a) stands in the onset verse's own bytes. The row's device_notes argue the bounds 'rather than from an imperative or addressee shift' and license that by 'the operative-category allowance'; re-read in the ruled strategy text, the operative-category law (§6) is a unit_type provision -- each vocabulary line names the operative category, any closed-vocabulary value applying wherever the row's own bytes carry that form, with a one-sentence deviation disclosure -- not a licence for a boundary driver, so the appeal is misapplied. The envelope is honest at its tiers: וְאֶל מִ֖י (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte) collates against oshb:Isa.40.25 at accent_stripped tier, while וְאֶל מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte) and וְאֶל מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי (oshb:Isa.40.25, tier: byte) return tier none against each other in both directions -- a matching two-token interrogative prefix, not a byte-identical refrain the refrain-close rule could carry the seam on by itself; observed_substrate_signals carries topic_onset, inclusio_bracket and postpositive_inquit, no addressee_shift. The filed finding weighed both sides; the complete test changes nothing and agrees with the prior adjudication's rule. Boundary byte-sound, warrant grounded on a non-ruled class with a misapplied law citation: confirm medium; one seam-pair edit cures this and the preceding row's close item; no span change.

Re-derived from bytes at MT 41:29|42:1, both sides. Preceding unit's close: הֵ֣ן כֻּלָּ֔ם אָ֥וֶן אֶ֖פֶס מַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.41.29, tier: byte) is the trial speech's verdict on the idols, its runs standing at exactly 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier -- no refrain, no closing formula, so the refrain-close rule (§6) gives no close-side warrant; the PE at MT 41:29 (single-witness inventory: PE at 41:29 and 42:4) is tier-3 corroboration, never a driver. Onset side: הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1, tier: byte) is a presentative onset of a new referent inside one continuing first-person divine speech. The trial speech's second-person-plural address is real -- רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם (oshb:Isa.41.21, tier: byte), הֵן אַתֶּ֣ם מֵאַ֔יִן (oshb:Isa.41.24, tier: byte), אִמְרֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.41.26, tier: byte) -- but its last form is that 41:26 suffix: MT 41:27-28 carry first-person forms, אֶתֵּֽן (oshb:Isa.41.27, tier: byte) and וְאֵ֨רֶא֙ with וְאֶשְׁאָלֵ֖ם (oshb:Isa.41.28, tier: byte), and MT 41:29 third-person-plural suffixes, מַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם and נִסְכֵּיהֶֽם (oshb:Isa.41.29, tier: byte), read against both witnesses (no morphology layer staged). The finding's replacement claim that the addressee is 'dropped at oshb:Isa.42.1' is therefore not supported: the drop falls at 41:27, three verses before the seam, and the seam carries no addressee change, no imperative, no vocative and no formula. What it carries is the presentative pair הֵ֣ן (oshb:Isa.41.29, tier: byte) answered by הֵ֤ן (oshb:Isa.42.1, tier: byte), collating at accent_stripped tier in both directions (verse-initial hen: 18 verses book-wide at skeleton tier; the two-token onset unique at 1 verse), with the referent turning from the idols' nothingness to the servant -- a referent/scene shift the docket must judge as a ruled explicit scene shift (§2a) or not. The row's onset warrant as shipped is a content characterisation plus the PE mark, no ruled class named, while its close at כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, tier: byte) is tier-1 and exact (sweep: 4 verses, the koh-amar formula in chs 41-43 at skeleton tier -- MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16; 48 book-wide; none of the four royal-messenger sites). Under the both-sides law neither side of 41:29|42:1 carries an uncontested ruled tier-1 signal; the finding is right that no ruled onset ground is named, and the servant_song value (§6) presupposes tier-1-argued bounds. Severity: not high -- the boundary is not byte-shown wrong, the row holds it at low confidence with the frontier flag on a held-classic zone (§7), and no load-bearing claim is byte-false; not low -- the sole onset warrant is a non-ruled class and the unit_type's own precondition is unmet. Confirm medium, agreeing with the prior adjudication's rule and its correction of the finding: the field repair must be re-cut to name the presentative onset of a new referent, with the PE as corroboration, rather than an addressee drop; the byte-grounded rival grouping from the summons at oshb:Isa.41.21 to the frame at 42:5 stays a docket question. No span change.

Re-derived from bytes at MT 42:25|43:1, both sides. The row's own close: וַתְּלַהֲטֵ֤הוּ מִסָּבִיב֙ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֔ע וַתִּבְעַר בּ֖וֹ וְלֹא יָשִׂ֥ים עַל לֵֽב (oshb:Isa.42.25, tier: byte) is third-person narration of the poured-out wrath, its runs at exactly 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier -- no refrain, no closing formula, so the refrain-close rule (§6) gives no close-side warrant; the PE at MT 42:25 (single-witness inventory: SAMEKH 42:17, PE 42:25) is tier-3 corroboration, never a driver. Following unit's onset: וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) is the divine-owned messenger formula, the ruled formula-onset class (§2a); the koh-amar skeleton stands at 48 verses book-wide and at exactly 4 in chs 41-43 (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier: MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16), all divine-owned since the royal-messenger sites are confined to MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16 and 37:3, and the verse-initial three-token onset is unique (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier). So the rear seam is warranted from the following unit's onset. The row as shipped: its entire close sentence is the PE, a programmatic skeleton scan of every field finds no koh-amar formula anywhere in the row, and its only engagement with MT 43:1 is the name-pair thread בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte) in device_notes, read stem-level against יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לְבֹזְזִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.42.24, tier: byte), which argues cohesion across the seam rather than a break. The filed finding already weighed both sides (the row's close and the next unit's onset); the complete test re-derives it unchanged and agrees with the prior adjudication's rule. Seam location byte-sound, mark claim byte-true, the seam-carrying signal absent from the record: confirm medium; field repair as proposed, no span change.

Re-derived from bytes at MT 45:25|46:1, both sides. Preceding unit's close: בַּיהוָ֛ה יִצְדְּק֥וּ וְיִֽתְהַלְל֖וּ כָּל זֶ֥רַע יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.45.25, tier: byte), a six-token third-person verdict closing the trial speech, its runs at exactly 1 verse book-wide at skeleton tier -- no refrain, no closing formula, so the refrain-close rule (§6) gives no close-side warrant; the single-witness inventory carries PE at MT 45:17, nothing at MT 45:18-46:1, SAMEKH at 46:2 (absence not counterevidence). Onset side: כָּרַ֥ע בֵּל֙ קֹרֵ֣ס נְב֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.46.1, tier: byte; tokens 1-4 of 12) opens on two suffix-conjugation verbs with freshly named subjects, turning from the first-person divine speech of MT 45:22-24 and the second-person summons of הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ (oshb:Isa.45.20, tier: byte) to a third-person tableau of Babylon's gods -- the ruled explicit scene-shift class (§2a), unique as a run (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier). So the front seam is warranted from its onset side and the row's cut is right. The row as shipped splices at MT 46:1 only נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1, tier: byte; tokens 9-10 of 12) and מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, tier: byte; tokens 11-12 of 12) -- the finding's 'only Hebrew spliced' undercounts by one run, neither run being the onset -- never splices the verse-initial onset, and neither its prose nor its boundary_evidence_refs carries MT 45:25 (verified programmatically against the shipped row), so the seam's preceding edge is uncharacterised and the front-seam warrant rides on the WEB quotation alone. The filed finding weighed both edges (onset unengaged, preceding close uncited); the complete test re-derives it unchanged and agrees with the prior adjudication's rule. A byte-unengaged, one-edged warrant on a byte-sound seam, more than a mechanical slip under the pointed-splice mandate for boundary-relevant claims: confirm medium; field repair as proposed, no span change.

Re-derived from bytes at MT 51:11|51:12, both sides -- and the row's own close side changes the outcome. Close side: the span ends on וּבָ֤אוּ צִיּוֹן֙ בְּרִנָּ֔ה וְשִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם עַל רֹאשָׁ֑ם שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ (oshb:Isa.51.11, tier: byte), a nine-token run byte-identical to oshb:Isa.35.10 and standing at exactly 2 verses book-wide at byte tier (MT 35:10, 51:11); the whole verses differ only at the plene/defective pair יְשׁוּב֗וּן (oshb:Isa.51.11, tier: byte) against יְשֻׁב֗וּן (oshb:Isa.35.10, tier: byte) and in the jointing of the final cola (whole-verse collation tier none), while the opening pair וּפְדוּיֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה and the closing pair יָג֥וֹן וַאֲנָחָֽה (oshb:Isa.51.11, tier: byte) re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Isa.35.10 as well; the pair שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ (oshb:Isa.51.11, tier: byte) stands at exactly 3 verses book-wide at byte tier (MT 35:10, 51:3, 51:11; accent-stripped and skeleton tiers add MT 22:13 for 4). At each byte site the pair opens the post-etnachta closing half of a verse that ends a marked paragraph -- PE at MT 35:10, the owner-ruled M3 frame end, SAMEKH at 51:3, SAMEKH at 51:11 (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration) -- so the bracket function is argued from bytes: this refrain closes units where it recurs, and under the strategy's refrain-close rule (§6) the row's own close carries a ruled close-side warrant. The row NAMES it: strongest_rejected_alternative calls שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ a portable refrain byte-identical at exactly 3 verses, names oshb:Isa.51.11 a near-twin of oshb:Isa.35.10, and reads its recurrence as 'this appeal's own closing cadence' -- a refrain-close argument, placed in the rejected-alternative field and aimed at the interior 51:10|51:11 question (verified programmatically: the pair's bytes stand in that field). Onset side: אָנֹכִ֧י אָנֹכִ֛י ה֖וּא מְנַחֶמְכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.51.12, tier: byte) is a verse-initial doubled first-person self-identification, a formula-class onset (sweep: 3 verses, verse-initial doubled anokhi at skeleton tier: MT 43:11, 43:25, 51:12; the three-token opening at 2 verses, MT 43:25 and 51:12; the pointed pair unique at byte tier), a speaker shift from the community's appeal to Yahweh's answer (§2a explicit scene shift); the row never names it and lists neither web:Isa.51.12 nor oshb:Isa.51.12 (verified against the shipped refs), while the next shipped row carries that onset as its own front-seam driver. The seam is thus warranted from both sides. The prior adjudication applied the onset-side test only -- 'the row's only stated back-seam warrant is a class that cannot warrant a seam' -- and did not weigh the close side; the complete test shows an admissible refrain-close driver present in the bytes and already in the row's own record, so the finding's 'no admissible driver' premise no longer holds. What remains is a placement-and-citation defect: the boundary field's back-seam sentence cites the tier-3 SAMEKH alone, the refrain-close argument sits in the wrong field framed for the interior question, and the forward verse is uncited. Downgrade to low. The proposed repair stands, widened: carry the refrain-close into boundary_rationale as the close-side driver, name the 51:12 self-identification onset, add web:Isa.51.12 and oshb:Isa.51.12 to boundary_evidence_refs, keep the SAMEKH as corroboration. No span change.
